name: Business Management and Marketing
overview: Seven semesters start from applied mathematics, marketing principles, management, finance, microeconomics and organizational behaviour, then move into digital marketing, e-commerce, consumer behaviour, neuromarketing, CRM, strategic and project management. You work on real company problems, build and launch an online shop, and run live ad campaigns for existing businesses. Two internships and a six-month thesis on a real organizational problem sit alongside a startup-conference study tour in Portugal and double-degree routes with BI Norwegian Business School or KEDGE. Graduates go into marketing, sales, consulting, project management or their own ventures.

name: Economics and Data Analytics
overview: Over seven semesters you combine economic theory (micro and macroeconomics, econometrics, international and public economics, behavioural economics) with mathematical analysis, programming, data science and an AI and machine learning course that works in Python. Applied work on real companies and two internships test the skills in practice, a three-day study tour to Brussels brings you to EU economists and institutions, and a bachelor thesis tackles a company problem. A double degree with BI Norwegian Business School is possible. Graduates work as economists, data and financial analysts, risk assessors or project managers.

name: Economics and Politics
overview: Economics, political science and business run through seven semesters: mathematical analysis and logic first, then comparative politics, the history of political ideas, econometrics and macroeconomics, and later political economy, public finance, international trade, welfare economics and applied game theory. Teaching leans on simulations such as policy wargaming and strategy modelling. Internships in public or private companies or non-governmental organizations and a thesis on a real company problem add practice, and a double degree with BI Norwegian Business School is open to selected students. Graduates become economists, strategists, diplomats, project managers or politicians.

name: Finance
overview: The core covers principles of finance, financial and advanced accounting, corporate finance, financial markets and institutions, investment management and risk management, supported by micro and macroeconomics, econometrics and international economics. Programming for finance and a FinTech course reflect the technology side, and you work with Bloomberg terminals. Two internships, in semesters five and seven, lead into a final bachelor thesis, and a double degree with BI Norwegian Business School is an option. Graduates work as financial analysts, investment managers, auditors, tax consultants or fintech entrepreneurs.

name: International Business and Communication
overview: Across seven semesters you study management, finance, marketing and economics, then international business, cross-cultural communication, international negotiations, global supply chains and strategic management, alongside communication theory, public relations and public speaking. Two internships with international companies and an interdisciplinary project give practical grounding, and the thesis is a consulting project for an international company. Double degrees are available with BI Norwegian Business School, KEDGE and BBA INSEEC-ECE. Graduates go into human resources, project and business development, marketing, sales and communications, or start their own companies.

name: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
overview: Six semesters mix business fundamentals (management, marketing, finance for startups, legal aspects, sales) with innovation modules such as design thinking, UX design and rapid prototyping, elements of artificial intelligence and digital business models. The learning runs through five consecutive business development projects ending in a Demo Day, plus challenge-based tasks from real organizations and two internships in startup settings. A three-month mentorship abroad for young entrepreneurs and semester exchanges are possible. Graduates become founders, product, marketing or project managers, and consultants.

name: International Business
overview: You start with economics, business mathematics and intercultural communication, then move through entrepreneurship, AI and innovation, management, marketing, enterprise and human resource management, international trade, supply chains and international negotiation. A professional internship and a business process simulation come in year two, and every student spends a semester at a partner university or in a foreign company. You choose one of two specialisations, E-Business or International Marketing, and a double degree with Thomas More in Belgium is possible. Studies run in stages rather than one big exam period. A final internship and project close the degree, and placements have included Teltonika Networks, Pigu and Hostinger.

name: Sales and Marketing
overview: The first year covers economics, business English, communication psychology and negotiation, then marketing, management, accounting, business models and creativity methods. Later modules cover brand and consumer experience, market research, trade management, supply chains and data analytics and pricing. A simulation and a professional internship in a company come in year two, and the last semester is a final internship and project. In year three you pick digital marketing communication with e-business or sales in B2B and B2C markets. Exchange semesters or placements are possible in countries such as Spain, Portugal, Germany and Finland. Graduates work as brand managers, sales managers and marketing specialists, or start businesses.

name: Tourism and Hotel Management
overview: After a first year of economics, tourism services and resources, travel geography, intercultural communication and tourism anthropology, you study management, marketing, accounting, business law and sustainable tourism business. Practice is a large part of the programme: a professional internship in a business enterprise in the second, fourth and sixth semesters, plus educational visits to hotels and attractions. In year three you choose either Tourism Management or Hotel Management. A double degree with LAB University of Applied Sciences in Finland is available. Graduates work in hotels, travel agencies, tourist information centres and wellness or leisure businesses.

name: English for Public Relations
overview: Alongside intensive English (grammar, phonetics, lexicology, stylistics, business English up to a professional level) you study social psychology, intercultural communication, organisational communication, sociolinguistics and public relations, plus a second foreign language from German, French, Russian, Spanish or Italian. Teaching is task-based and group-based. Internships in media outlets, cultural and social service centres and private companies run through three semesters, and the degree ends with content localisation and a final thesis. Short study or placement periods are possible in Portugal, Spain, Belgium, Turkey, Ireland and Latvia, and a double degree with the University of Tirana is offered.

name: Multimedia Technology
overview: Early semesters mix mathematics, graphic design, computer graphics, electronics, cybersecurity and programming. Later you add video and audio technology, electronic publishing, 2D animation, 3D modelling and animation, media communication and media business management. Practical training is central, with two multimedia product design courses run as internships, a final internship and a thesis. The profile leans toward digital content, interface design and interactive media. Graduates work as digital content creators, UI and UX designers, animation and 3D designers or virtual and augmented reality developers in agencies, start-ups, game studios and TV.

name: Software systems
overview: The degree builds from Java, Python, C#, algorithms, databases, web design and networks into .NET, software testing, mobile programming, cloud computing and cyber security. A course project each semester takes you from a single-user system to client-server and heterogeneous systems, a long programming practice follows in year three, and a final internship and thesis finish the degree. In the sixth semester you choose between a machine learning engineering route and an internet-of-things route. Graduates work as software designers and analysts, programmers, testers and project managers, and can continue to a master's in informatics in Lithuania or abroad.

name: General Practice Nursing
overview: Seven semesters combine anatomy, physiology, pharmacology and microbiology with general, surgical, therapeutic, geriatric, mental health, emergency and intensive, children's, maternity, palliative and community nursing. Much of the time is clinical: simulation classes with mannequins and acted situations, then professional internships in primary care centres and in second- and third-level hospital departments. Study or placement periods abroad are possible through Erasmus+, and a double diploma with XAMK in Finland is offered. A final internship and thesis close the degree. Graduates work as nurses in hospitals, clinics, doctors' and nurses' practices and community settings.

name: Applied Chemistry
overview: The early semesters cover mathematics, physics, inorganic and organic chemistry, cell biology and physical chemistry, followed by chemical analysis, polymer and colloid chemistry, biochemistry, instrumental analysis, functional materials and process engineering. Later options reach into cosmetics chemistry, drug chemistry and technology, toxicology and sustainable chemistry. Laboratory work is constant, and you can join research groups from the first year, complete a product development project and two internships. Two pathways are offered, Innovation Development with industry partners or Pedagogy for a teaching qualification. Graduates work as chemists and quality control specialists in pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, materials and energy.

name: Biomedical Materials Industries
overview: The course draws on chemistry, biology and engineering: organic, physical and polymer chemistry sit beside cell and molecular biology, human anatomy, tissue engineering, biomedical materials science and process engineering. Instrumental analysis, toxicology and risk assessment and good manufacturing practice prepare you for industry. You work in specialised laboratories, complete a product development project, two internships and a final project. Pathways in Innovation Development or Pedagogy are available, and exchange partners include Aveiro and the Technical University of Denmark. Graduates develop biomedical materials and technologies or work as experts and researchers in companies such as Thermo Fisher Scientific.

name: Chemical Technology and Engineering
overview: The first years build mathematics, physics, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry, chemical analysis, engineering graphics and general chemical technology, then move on to instrumental analysis, materials science, process engineering, process modelling and chemical thermodynamics. The final year brings chemical engineering design, a project practicum, a professional internship and the bachelor thesis. You work in process research and control laboratories and choose between Organic Materials (plastics, elastomers, refining, paper and textiles) and Inorganic Materials (acids, fertilizers, ceramics, glass). A double degree with the University of Carthage is possible. Graduates work as technologists and project engineers, including in hydrogen and renewable energy.

name: Food Science and Technology
overview: Chemistry (inorganic, organic, physical), biology, mathematics and physics lead into food chemistry and analysis, food microbiology and hygiene, food technologies, sensory evaluation, nutrition and metabolism, and food quality and safety. Electives include sustainable food systems, toxicology and molecular gastronomy. You work in laboratories with analytical and pilot-scale equipment, on product development projects and real technological cases with industry practitioners, and complete two internships. Learning routes are challenge-based learning, Innovation Development or Pedagogy. Exchange partners include Wageningen and the Technical University of Denmark. Graduates become food technologists, quality controllers, nutritionists or product developers.

name: Industrial Biotechnology
overview: Over eight semesters mathematics, physics, chemistry, cell biology and microbiology lead into molecular biology, genetic engineering, bioinformatics, instrumental analysis and bioprocess engineering, then enzymology, polymer chemistry, biotechnology equipment design and process optimisation. You experiment hands-on with micro-organisms, yeast, plant and algal cells in laboratories, take on a product development project, and finish with a professional internship and a bachelor thesis project. An Innovation Development or Pedagogy pathway is optional, and Erasmus+ exchanges include Wageningen and Padova. Graduates work as bioproduct production technologists, quality assurance specialists and innovation coordinators.

name: Architecture
overview: This integrated five-year programme runs studio-based design from fundamentals through residential and public buildings and building complexes to landscape design, alongside building physics, structures, BIM, energy performance, construction planning, architectural history and theory, heritage and urban planning. You work in close contact with lecturers and on joint projects with civil engineering students. A long professional internship in the sixth semester, research projects and a master thesis complete the degree. You choose between building design, landscape architecture and urban planning. Graduates become architects, urbanists or landscape architects, and the diploma allows practice across the EU.

name: Automation and Control
overview: Eight semesters build from physics, mathematics, programming and circuit analysis to automatic control theory, electric drives, instrumentation and logical automation, with modules on artificial intelligence, computer vision and digital twins. From the fifth semester you specialise in Control Systems, Mechatronic Systems or Process Control. Practical work uses laboratories and real industrial equipment, and the last semester combines a professional internship with the final project. Exchange partners include Aalto, Lund and Hiroshima. Graduates work as control systems engineers and designers and automation systems programmers.

name: Electrical Engineering
overview: After physics, mathematics, programming and engineering materials, you study electric circuits, electromechanics, applied and power electronics, high voltage engineering, automatic control, electric drives, electrical networks and power system elements. You specialise in either Energy Converters and Control or Information Technology of Electrical Engineering, and can add an Innovation Development path or a Pedagogy minor. Laboratories include distributed generation and power plant facilities, a product development project comes in semester six, and an internship and thesis project end the degree. Exchange partners include DTU, Lund and Linkoping. Graduates work in power generation, distribution and smart grids.

name: Electronics and Electrical Engineering
overview: Six semesters cover mathematics, physics, circuit theory, signal processing, analogue, digital and power electronics, microprocessor systems with embedded programming, power systems and smart grids, and measurement. Teaching happens in numerous teaching laboratories and FabLab Kaunas, with guest lectures from industry. A product development project comes in semester four, and a professional internship and final project close the degree. Exchange partners include Korea University and Vienna University of Technology. The mix of electronics and power leads to roles as electronics or electrical engineers or smart systems architects, and on to postgraduate study in either field.

name: Renewable Energy Engineering
overview: Physics, mathematics, programming, thermodynamics and circuit analysis lead to electrical machines for renewable sources, power engineering, heat transfer and control theory, with topics on solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, heat pumps, biomass, fuel cells, energy storage and nuclear fundamentals. You train in laboratories with Siemens and ABB equipment and in the storage and smart grid centres, with mandatory placements at energy companies, visits to power facilities and a final project. Two tracks are offered, Smart Electric Power Systems or Sustainable Thermal Energy Systems. Graduates work as renewable energy integration specialists, thermal energy engineers or digital transformation specialists.

name: Robotics
overview: Eight semesters combine physics, mathematics, programming and circuit analysis with control technologies, electromechanics, robot kinematics and dynamics, microprocessors, image processing, intelligent control, robot programming and simulation, plus AI ethics. You learn in robotics laboratories and the Rockwell Automation Training Centre, build object models and run simulations with robot digital twins, and hear from companies such as ABB, Omron and Elinta Robotics. A professional internship and a bachelor thesis project finish the course. Innovation Development and Pedagogy pathways are open, with exchanges to Hiroshima and DTU. Graduates work as robotics engineers, system designers and robot programmers.

name: Transport Electronics
overview: You study mathematics, physics, electronics, circuit theory, programming in Matlab, Python and C++, signals and systems, microprocessors and automotive electronic systems, with emphasis on transport sensors and testing and diagnostic systems. Further topics include embedded design, autonomous vehicle control, traffic flow control and AI in electronic systems. Teams design and build working prototypes in semester projects, and the university has an advanced automotive diagnostics laboratory. The last semester combines a professional internship with the bachelor final project. Graduates work as transport electronics, diagnostic and maintenance engineers or design engineers for autonomous transport systems.

name: Artificial Intelligence
overview: You start with object-oriented programming, mathematics, digital logic, databases, data structures and discrete structures, then study machine learning, deep learning, image processing, speech recognition, cloud computing for AI, multi-agent systems, computer architecture, operating systems and software engineering. Lectures from active researchers are mixed with practitioner guest talks, a team-based product development project comes in semester six, and an internship in semester eight finishes the degree. Innovation Development lets you build products with partners, and exchange partners include Deusto and Bologna. Graduates work as AI solutions developers, AI systems analysts and developers of human-assisted intelligent systems.

name: Informatics
overview: Eight semesters cover object-oriented programming, mathematics, digital logic, data structures, computer architecture, databases, operating systems, algorithms, software engineering, networks and concurrent programming. From the fifth semester you specialise in Internet Informatics (web applications, cloud, network security) or Multimedia Systems (visual design, 3D modelling, digital audio and video, virtual reality), with optional depth in machine learning, cryptography or data analytics. A product development project with partners in semester six, access to high-performance computing, and a final internship and project make up the practice. Graduates work as software developers, systems analysts or digital twinning engineers.

name: Engineering Physics
overview: The core is chemistry, mathematics, classical mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics and statistical physics, quantum mechanics and solid state physics, applied through Python programming, computer-aided design, electronics, machine learning, optics and light technologies and metrology. Electives can lead toward nuclear and particle physics or computational intelligence. You work in modern laboratories, complete a product development project in semester six, then an engineering internship and a final project. Innovation Development and Pedagogy pathways are open, and exchanges include DTU and Aveiro. Graduates work as engineering technologists, renewable energy technologists or quantum systems metrologists.

name: Materials Physics and Nanotechnologies
overview: Over four years you study chemistry, mathematics, classical and quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, electrodynamics, solid state physics, nuclear and particle physics and the physics of materials, then micro- and nanotechnology, thin films, functional materials and nanophotonics. Teaching is built around smart laboratories where students research alongside lecturers, a product development project and a final bachelor project, plus a professional internship. Routes include challenge-based learning, Innovation Development and Pedagogy, with Erasmus+ exchanges in Denmark, Portugal, China and South Korea. Graduates work as materials engineers, quantum computer technicians or nanorobot engineers, or continue to master's and doctoral research.

name: Aviation Engineering
overview: Mathematics, physics, chemistry, engineering drawing and CAD lead into aerodynamics, aircraft types and systems, unmanned aerial vehicles, aviation materials, avionics and aviation engines, with thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, structural integrity, human factors and air law alongside. Learning is problem- and project-based, with student projects such as a flying aerodynamics laboratory and a human-powered aircraft, laboratory work with licensed aviation professionals, and a final-year internship. You choose between Aircraft Design and Aircraft Technical Maintenance. Exchanges include IPSA in France and Limerick. Graduates work as aircraft designers, aeronautical technologists or hybrid electric aircraft developers in design, repair and aerospace companies.

name: Fashion Engineering
overview: You combine mathematics, physics, chemistry and materials science with textile technologies, clothing pattern construction, fashion design and digital tools such as Lectra, Gerber CAD and Adobe Creative Suite, and later functional textiles, textile recycling, knit design and virtual fashion creation. Teaching includes pattern modelling, prototyping and garment construction in labs, digital design studios, company visits and real-world cases, with exchange semesters at European partners such as Boras and Liberec. A bachelor thesis or professional internship ends the degree, and electives let you lean toward design, marketing, business or virtual fashion. Graduates work as clothing designers, textile experts or virtual fashion specialists.

name: Industrial Engineering
overview: The programme covers mathematics, physics, engineering mechanics, thermodynamics, electrotechnics, materials science of metals, ceramics and polymers, CAD, quality assurance, ergonomics and manufacturing technologies, then additive manufacturing, Industry 4.0 and robotic systems. Laboratory work combines with product development projects, semester-long capstones and a work placement in Lithuanian or international companies. You choose between Digital Manufacturing and Production and Manufacturing Management, and can follow an extended-internship route. Exchanges include the Technical University of Denmark and Southern Denmark. Graduates work as process improvement specialists, sustainable production project managers or autonomous factory developers.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: You begin with mathematics, physics, chemistry, engineering drawing, thermodynamics, mechanics and materials science, then CAD, machine dynamics, manufacturing engineering and structural integrity. From year two you choose Biomechanics, Mechanical Systems Design, Robotics Engineering or Thermal Systems Engineering. Learning uses laboratories with GUNT systems, CNC machines, Festo robotic kits and 3D prototyping, software such as SolidWorks and Autodesk Inventor, and real engineering problems solved through modelling and optimisation. A mandatory work placement and final project fall in year four, with routes for deeper specialisation, innovation development or extended practice. Graduates work as design engineers, production technologists or biomechanical engineers.

name: Mechatronics
overview: Mechanics, electronics and programming are taught together across eight semesters, through mathematics, physics, engineering drawing, CAD, thermodynamics, electronics, control systems, robotics and manufacturing technologies. Laboratories include Festo production lines, 3D printers, ABB robots and CNC machine tools, and semester projects have you solve real problems and build working prototypes. Professional internships and a capstone project complete the degree, an Innovation Development pathway lets you build products with partners, and exchanges include Chalmers and Tampere. Graduates work as automated systems engineers, robotics engineers or digital twin developers in manufacturing, aerospace, biomedical and automation sectors.

name: Communication Studies and Information Management Technologies
overview: Six semesters cover communication theories, organisational and political communication, public relations, risk and crisis communication, audiovisual production, data journalism and information systems design, with research methods, data and text analytics, graphic design, digital marketing and interface design. Academic English at C1 level and creative and media writing sit alongside electives such as media psychology. You work on product development projects and communication campaigns and complete a semester-long internship and a final project. The programme runs as a twin degree with the University of Twente in the Netherlands. Graduates work in communications and marketing, content development and information management.

name: New Media Language
overview: You study linguistics, media culture, discourse analysis and applied linguistics together with writing for different platforms: academic, creative, technical and web content, plus video and audio editing and public speaking. English is taken to C1 level, and you add a second language from French, German, Russian, Spanish or Swedish. Practical work includes creating digital content with Adobe tools and WordPress, challenge-based tasks, a product development project, a professional internship and a bachelor thesis. Exchange routes run through the Applied European Languages network with Spain and France. Graduates work as digital media strategists, content developers, transmedia storytellers, social media managers and digital marketers.

name: Public Policy and Administration
overview: The curriculum covers political theory, comparative politics, international relations, administrative law and public governance, with modules on Eastern European politics, European Union policy, public finance management, the civil service, and ethics and corruption prevention, plus research methods and digital transformation of the public sector. You work in interdisciplinary teams on a product development project, complete a professional internship and write a final project. Electives let you lean toward Local and Regional Government or Political Communication and Technology. Graduates work as policy analysts, project managers or civil servants, or continue to master's study in political science, public administration, sociology or management.

name: Business Digitalization Management
overview: Eight semesters start with informatics, mathematics and economics, then management, accounting, financial management, marketing and human resources, combined with databases, programming, business intelligence, data mining and process automation. Specialist topics include project, change and innovation management, digital marketing and artificial intelligence in business. Teaching uses challenge-based learning, business simulations and the DigiLab with UiPath software, and an internship of up to a year in Lithuanian or international companies falls in semesters six and seven, followed by a final project. Graduates work as business analysts, digitisation project managers or digital transformation specialists.

name: Economics
overview: Core study covers microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics, accounting, finance and data analytics, supported by mathematics, statistics, marketing, business law and the history of economic thought. Case studies, business simulations and professional tools such as Bloomberg, SPSS and EViews bring theory into practice, and you can earn a Bloomberg Market Concepts certificate. Product development projects with researchers and business partners and an internship in semester eight complete the degree, and competency blocks let you add accounting and analytics, management, financial mathematics, languages, neuroscience or public governance. Graduates work as economists, consultants and data analysts in finance, government and business.

name: Chemical Engineering (Environment and Energy)
overview: The core subjects are process engineering, process and equipment simulation, design of technological processes, environmental technology and renewable energy sources, taught with an interdisciplinary view of emerging research areas. The aim is to analyse and develop chemical and technological processes and to work in a fast-changing chemical industry. Graduates can also apply this knowledge in environmental protection departments and nature conservation bodies, and the university offers related master's programmes in innovative processes engineering and production engineering.

name: Electrical Engineering
overview: You study electrical circuits, electrical machines and drives, information technologies, industrial controls and communication, electricity and renewable energy, and microcontrollers. Courses include robotic systems, renewable energetics and energy efficiency, microprocessors, programmable logic controllers and electrical transport systems, with a focus on designing, programming, maintaining and operating industrial automation equipment. Graduates can work in electronics, electric power, transport, automation and robotics, renewable energy and electrical system design, and a related master's programme in innovative electrical and automation systems is available.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: The curriculum includes an introduction to mechanical engineering, computer-aided structural design, automatic control of mechatronic systems, computerised design of processing technologies and environmental engineering. You learn to work in teams and with other specialists to create working devices, robots and machines, using modern computer design programmes. Graduates become design engineers, consultants, experts or department heads in industries such as furniture, textiles, chemicals and recycling, and some move into laboratory research. Related master's programmes are production engineering and innovative processes engineering.

name: Marine Transport Engineering
overview: Marine engineering is combined with IT infrastructure, with courses in the basics of ship design, ship hydro-aeromechanics, marine environmental protection technologies, shipbuilding and repair technology, and business and engineering project management. The specialisation is Naval Architecture and Shipbuilding, which develops skills in ship design and digital innovation and addresses the environmental standards of the International Maritime Organization. Graduates work as constructors, ship architects, engineers or project managers in shipbuilding design, construction and repair, and can continue to the master's programme in shipping and port engineering.

name: Port Technology Management
overview: You learn to manage port technologies, use computerised IT systems and solve logistics problems, with attention to smart autonomous ports and e-logistics. Graduates work as engineers in maritime and transport sectors, port administration, stevedoring, ship agency and freight forwarding, in roles such as technical consultant, industrial manager or project manager, or as entrepreneurs. The degree leads on to master's study, with shipping and port engineering offered as a related option at the same university.

name: Informatics
overview: The subjects include artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, web technologies and digital graphics, computer networks and the internet of things, object-oriented programming, computer architecture and operating systems, data mining and simulation modelling. Graduates can work as software developers, data analysts, cybersecurity analysts, AI and machine learning engineers, web developers, UX designers or researchers, in sectors such as healthcare, finance, e-commerce and government.

name: Physical Geography and Oceanography
overview: The subjects are oceanography, remote sensing methods, GIS, hydrology, and meteorology and climatology, applied to marine and environmental questions. Practice includes field work on the university's marine research vessel and technologies from drones to satellite image analysis for monitoring the environment. Graduates interpret natural, climatic and social phenomena in practice and work in nature protection and other environmental institutions or in hydrometeorological services.

name: Economics
overview: Courses include micro- and macroeconomics, economic policy, regional and European economics, enterprise economics, the service economy, economic analysis and modelling, environmental economics, finance and investment, marketing, project management, corporate social responsibility and taxation. You apply theory, research and data analysis skills to real-world issues. Graduates work as economists in the public, private and non-profit sectors, and the university offers related master's degrees in business management and regional governance.

name: Management
overview: The curriculum covers crisis management, business analytics, e-business, business ethics and social responsibility, and entrepreneurship, combining theory with practice and taught by academics and practitioners of management. Graduates can start their own business or work as functional managers in personnel, finance, production or marketing. A related master's programme in business management is available for further study.

name: Recreation and Tourism
overview: Main courses include leadership and change management, resort, spa and wellness studies, tourism structure and resources, and recreation and tourism management and planning. You choose between two specialisations, Health Tourism and E-Tourism. Graduates work as managers in travel agencies, accommodation and recreation businesses, tourism information centres, national and regional park administrations and municipalities, or set up their own businesses; about a tenth work abroad. Related master's programmes include business management and health care management.

name: Social Work and Crisis Intervention
overview: The programme focuses on crisis intervention methods and social work practice: managing difficult situations and giving timely help to socially disadvantaged people and groups, with emphasis on the personal strength and leadership of a future social worker. Graduates work in municipal social support departments, addiction centres, homes for the elderly or children, social service centres, NGOs, health care institutions and hospitals, and can continue in social work, health care management, public administration, social pedagogy or management.

name: English Philology
overview: The subjects include English language and lexicology, introduction to linguistics, the history and culture of Great Britain, intercultural communication, English stylistics, trends in modern linguistics, literary and linguistics seminars, and translation theory and practice, with a second foreign language chosen from Swedish, Spanish or German. Graduates work in municipal government, chambers of commerce, insurance, tourism, media translation departments and marine organisations, and can continue to a master's in linguistics.

name: History of Europe
overview: You study the histories of European regions from the Mediterranean to the Baltic and from west to east, together with applied subjects such as heritage communication, geopolitics, climate change and digital humanities, and themes including conflict resolution, human rights, migration, nationalism and epidemics. Teaching is in small groups, mixing on-campus and online courses, and builds research, dissemination and communication skills. Graduates go into education, research, museums, archives and libraries, heritage conservation, journalism, public affairs and teaching.

name: Public Health
overview: The programme covers assessing population health, preventing disease and injury, developing health promotion programmes, epidemiology including outbreak control, vaccination programmes and organising preventive care. Graduates work in municipal health departments, public health offices and centres, health promotion units, primary health care institutions and specialised care facilities, and as public health specialists in educational institutions. A related master's programme in public health education is available.

name: Leisure Sports
overview: You choose one of four tracks: basketball, football, sports dances or leisure sports. Coursework covers sports pedagogy and training methods, from movement control and training basketball players to coaching and elite youth football development, standard and Latin American dance, and agility games, gymnastics and adult fitness. Courses are partly hybrid, and partners include the Lithuanian Basketball Federation, FC Barcelona methodology and the Lithuanian Football Federation, which offers UEFA coaching licences during studies. Graduates earn a physical education teaching qualification and work as coaches, fitness specialists, teachers and personal trainers.

name: International Business Administration
overview: The four years move from critical thinking and business fundamentals through management functions, accounting, marketing and information systems to business research, organisational behaviour and electives in economics, marketing or leadership. Core courses include micro- and macroeconomics, financial and management accounting, statistics, business finance and entrepreneurship, with a focus on the European and global economy and Eastern Europe in particular. A supervised business practicum in year four and a thesis defended in public finish the degree. Graduates move into management, finance, marketing, human resources or their own enterprise, or on to graduate study.

name: Global Business and Communication
overview: Business management courses (financial accounting, marketing, business finance, economics) sit beside liberal arts courses in arts, history, natural sciences and ethics, and communication electives such as media literacy, public relations, web and graphic design, social media management, brand management and marketing communication. Classes are small, with about sixteen students per teacher, and the emphasis is on practical experience. The degree blends creativity with business management for careers in marketing, social media and digital marketing, product and brand management and public relations.

name: Contemporary Communication
overview: The curriculum spans communication and media fundamentals, interpersonal communication, video production, media theory, public relations, media writing, web design, rhetorical analysis, persuasion and propaganda, cultural communication and conflict resolution, with leadership and ethics throughout. You make video productions, complete an internship in year four with a local or international business, and carry out a capstone project on a communication theme of your choice. Classes are small. Graduates work in public relations, advertising, social media, government and business communication, media production and NGOs, or continue to graduate study in communication.

name: English Language and Literature
overview: Core courses cover written composition, literature, linguistics, TESOL methods, translation and interpretation, expository writing, language research methods and ethics, set within a liberal arts frame that includes world civilizations. Workshops and writing assignments are complemented by practicum courses such as teaching in summer camps or schools, editorial work or submitting literary work for publication. In year four you write a thesis with a faculty mentor and defend it in public. Tracks lean toward English teaching, translation and literary studies, and graduates work in teaching, translation, marketing and administration or continue to graduate study.

name: International Relations and Development
overview: You study political science, international relations, development theory, economics and research methodology, together with political philosophy, conflict studies, negotiation, project management and intercultural communication. Research is built in from the start: a research proposal in year one, primary data collection in years three and four, and an independent thesis project at the end. Two supervised practicum courses place you in real-world work settings. Classes are small. Graduates work in diplomatic missions, public institutions, NGOs, development cooperation, human rights organisations and research institutes, or continue to graduate study.

name: Psychology
overview: The four years run from introduction to psychology, human development and interpersonal communication, through social and biological psychology, research methods and statistics, health psychology, cognition and introduction to clinical psychology, to abnormal psychology, counselling, neuropsychology, psychological assessment, then educational and organisational psychology. Practicum I in year two and a supervised Practicum II in an approved agency in year four give field experience, and an individual research thesis closes the degree. Graduates go into graduate study in clinical, counselling, educational or organisational psychology and neuropsychology, or work in social services, human resources and education.

name: Evangelical Theology
overview: The programme centres on biblical literature (Old and New Testament, the Pentateuch, the Synoptic Gospels), Christian theology, the history of Christianity, apologetics and worldview, with philosophy, ethics, missiology, peacemaking and justice. First-year seminars are interactive and group-based, two Christian ministry practicum courses come with instructor guidance, and year four includes research methods and a supervised thesis defended in public. Classes are small. Graduates are prepared for theological graduate study, ministry in churches and service organisations, teaching, or professional careers that draw on a liberal arts education.

name: Music Performance: Piano
overview: Your principal instrument, the piano, is studied in every semester, supported by piano accompaniment, sight-reading, piano ensemble and chamber ensemble. Alongside it run ear training and music theory (or harmony, polyphony and analysis), the language of music from the Middle Ages to the twentieth century, the history of piano art and of Lithuanian music and culture. Professional practice builds experience, and the degree ends with a final art project, a piano accompaniment project and a chamber ensemble project, each defended in public.

name: Music Performance: String Instruments
overview: The degree centres on a principal string instrument (violin, viola, cello, double bass, harp or guitar), studied through seven semesters. Orchestra life is built in through symphony orchestra and orchestral parts and sight-reading, and chamber music is compulsory, with a string quartet for violin, viola and cello players. Theory, ear training, music analysis, the history of string instruments and of Lithuanian music complete the core, followed by professional practice and a final art project plus a chamber ensemble project.

name: Music Performance: Wind and Percussion
overview: You specialise in one wind or percussion instrument (flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon, saxophone, horn, trumpet, trombone, tuba, baritone, euphonium, cornet or percussion), studied every semester. A large share of the study goes to ensemble and orchestra work: wind quintet, equal-voice or chamber ensembles, symphony, wind or brass band orchestras, and percussion ensembles. Basics of conducting, the history of wind instruments and percussion, theory and music history sit alongside, and professional practice leads to a final art project and an ensemble art project.

name: Music Performance: Vocal Performance
overview: Vocal performance is studied in every semester together with chamber vocal performance, the phonetics of foreign languages, Italian, stage speech, stage movement, acting and dance, plus piano as a secondary instrument. Theory, ear training, music history, the history of vocal art and of Lithuanian music complete the core. Stage experience comes through opera practice and professional practice, and the degree ends with an opera art project, a chamber singing art project and a final art project.

name: Music Performance: Jazz
overview: The principal instrument or voice (accordion, bass guitar, vocals, flute, piano, guitar, clarinet, double bass, percussion, saxophone, trumpet or trombone) is taught alongside jazz improvisation, jazz harmony and rhythmics, arranging, the basics of jazz composition and jazz history. You play in an ensemble and in a big band (vocalists sing in a jazz choir), and learn digital notation and sound recording equipment. A secondary instrument, professional practice, a final art project and an ensemble art project round it off.

name: Music Performance: Accordion
overview: Accordion is studied as the principal instrument across the degree, with chamber ensemble, accordion orchestra, basics of conducting and instrumentation. Core academic subjects include ear training and music theory, harmony, analysis, music history, the history of accordion art and of Lithuanian music and culture. Professional practice builds experience and the degree closes with a final art project and a chamber ensemble art project.

name: Music Performance: Organ
overview: Organ is the principal instrument, joined by a sacred music studio (choir, Latin, sacred music history, choir conducting, liturgics and liturgy practice), basso continuo, improvisation, the structure and tuning of the organ, chamber ensemble and accompaniment, and a secondary choice of harpsichord, piano or voice. Theory, music history and the history of organ art and of Lithuanian music complete the study. Professional practice and a final art project plus a chamber ensemble and accompaniment project close the degree.

name: Music Performance: Harpsichord
overview: The harpsichord is studied for seven semesters, with a secondary instrument (piano or organ), chamber ensemble, the structure and tuning of the harpsichord, basso continuo and figured bass. Supporting subjects include ear training, harmony, polyphony and musical analysis, the history of harpsichord art, music history alternatives and the history of Lithuanian music and culture, with philosophy and aesthetics. Professional practice leads to a chamber ensemble art project and a defended final art project.

name: Music Performance: Choir Conducting
overview: Choir conducting is the main subject, together with choir score reading, choir singing, vocal performance, choral arrangement, choral conducting theory and piano for choir conductors. The history of Lithuanian and European choral music broadens the picture. Professional practice has two routes, conducting a children's choir or a church choir, the latter with organ, liturgy and Gregorian chant, and the degree ends with a final art project.

name: Music Performance: Wind Orchestra Conducting
overview: Conducting is studied through seven semesters together with a wind instrument, wind orchestra playing, score reading, instrumentation and piano. Ear training, the language of music across the periods and Lithuanian music history provide the background. Practice is central: professional practice, a dedicated practice in conducting a wind orchestra, and a final art project at the end of the degree.

name: Music Performance: Symphony Orchestra Conducting
overview: Conducting is the main subject through all semesters, supported by score reading, instrumentation, piano, ear training and the language of music across the periods. Specialist subjects include the musical articulation of the string group in a symphony orchestra and orchestra music styles, and a symphony orchestra conducting practice runs over several semesters. Lithuanian music history, professional practice and a final art project complete the degree.

name: Music Studies: Composition
overview: The composition specialisation combines individual lessons and practice in composing with a composition theory studio and seminars, orchestration, instruments and score, piano, ear training and conducting, and music technology literacy. Analysis and composing principles, contexts of music and sound, music history and Lithuanian music history sit alongside, plus electives such as music and performer management, project management, public relations and copyright. A practice of implementing art projects leads to a final bachelor's project.

name: Music Studies: Electronic Music
overview: The electronic music specialisation is built around individual lessons and practice in electronic music, an electronic music studio and ensemble, virtual instruments, arrangement and electronic music seminars, with music technology literacy and ear training and conducting. Analysis and composing principles, contexts of music and sound and music history frame the practice, with electives in music and performer management, project management, public relations and copyright. A practice of implementing art projects leads to a final bachelor's project.

name: Music Studies: Music and Education
overview: The music and education specialisation combines music (piano, ear training, musical computer technologies, analysis and composing principles, music history) with pedagogy: introduction to art pedagogy, pedagogical and developmental psychology, creative pedagogy, and methodology and practice in preschool, primary and secondary music education. Pedagogical practice and observation of modern education strategies put this into practice, and the study ends with a final thesis of pedagogical studies alongside the bachelor's project.

name: Dance: Classical
overview: The classical dance specialisation is organised around dance praxis and creation and dance theory and discourses through most of the degree, with voice and acting praxis, sound and space contexts, and professional sustainability and practice running throughout. Philosophy, aesthetics, project management and the psychology of art and creativity add the wider context, and the degree ends with a final art project that is defended.

name: Dance: Contemporary
overview: The contemporary dance specialisation is organised around dance praxis and creation and dance theory and discourses through most of the degree, with voice and acting praxis, sound and space contexts, and professional sustainability and practice running throughout. Philosophy, aesthetics, project management and the psychology of art and creativity add the wider context, and the degree ends with a final art project that is defended.

name: Dance and Education
overview: Core study covers classical dance, a dance lab, dance composition and improvisation, the history of dance art, world dance, historical dance and costume, anatomy and injury prevention, anthropology of dance and dance management. You choose one of three styles: ballroom dance, folk dance (including song festival dance composition) or performative dance. A minor in pedagogy brings art pedagogy, psychology, subject teaching methodology and pedagogical practice, ending in a final project and a pedagogical thesis.

name: Medicine
overview: The first year covers anatomy, histology, genetics, physics and chemistry, followed by systems-based modules on reproduction and inheritance, neuroscience, immune response and infection, respiration and circulation, metabolism and locomotion, and the fundamentals of preclinical study. Years four to six are clinical modules and clinical practice. Teaching is problem-based, solving clinical cases in small groups of up to ten, with simulation equipment for practical skills and placements at the Baltic region's largest clinical hospital and other accredited hospitals across Lithuania. Research basics run through the curriculum and Erasmus+ exchanges are possible. Graduates qualify as medical doctors.

name: Odontology
overview: Foundation sciences such as anatomy, histology and embryology, biochemistry and physiology fill the first two years, then clinical specialities follow: cariology, endodontics, oral and maxillofacial surgery, orthodontics, periodontology and oral mucosal disease, prosthetic dentistry and paediatric dentistry, each with clinical practice. Teaching is problem-based, with simulation facilities and clinical training in groups of up to ten at the region's largest hospital system. Erasmus+ exchanges are available. Graduates can practise as dentists, go into residency or PhD programmes, or work in research and public health.

name: Pharmacy
overview: The first two years build biology, mathematics, physics, anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology, then pharmaceutical sciences: organic and analytical chemistry, pharmacognosy, pharmaceutical chemistry and technology, pharmacology, toxicology, clinical pharmacy and pharmacotherapy, pharmaceutical care, biotechnology and biopharmaceutics. Teaching is problem-based, in renovated laboratories with simulation equipment, and practical training takes place in public and hospital pharmacies. Erasmus+ exchanges for a semester or a year are possible. Graduates qualify as pharmacists.

name: Veterinary Medicine
overview: Years one and two cover anatomy, histology, embryology and animal physiology, with husbandry, welfare, cell biology, microbiology and genetics. Years three and four add propaedeutics, pharmacology, pathology, toxicology, parasitology, immunology and epidemiology, and the last two years turn to diagnostic imaging, surgery on large and small animals, internal diseases, obstetrics, forensic medicine and food hygiene. Teaching combines theory, clinical practice and research in laboratories with simulation equipment, in clinical groups of up to ten. Graduates work in state food and veterinary services or private practice, or continue to a PhD or residency.

name: Nursing
overview: Over four years you move from humanitarian-social and biomedical sciences, healthcare fundamentals and nursing techniques to nursing theory and introductory clinical subjects, then adult nursing, pedagogy, nursing administration and research methods, and finally specialised and geriatric nursing with final clinical examinations and a thesis defence. Teaching is problem-based, with simulation equipment, small clinical groups and placements at the region's largest hospital in departments such as oncology, neurology and interventional radiology. Erasmus+ exchanges are available. Graduates work as general practice nurses at all levels of care or continue to a master's.

name: Occupational Therapy
overview: Year one combines philosophy, ethics, psychology, anatomy, cytology, genetics and first aid with occupational therapy theory and models and first practice. Later years cover occupational therapy for older people, physiology, pathology, biomechanics and rehabilitation, then mental health and activity disorders, community-based therapy, healthcare system management, research methodology and a bachelor's thesis. Practice is extensive, with more than a thousand hours in real settings, in small groups and taught by practising occupational therapists. Graduates work in hospitals, rehabilitation institutions, nursing homes and wellness services, or continue to master's and doctoral study.

name: Physiotherapy
overview: The first year covers anatomy, physiology, cytology, genetics, psychology and the principles of physiotherapy, then biochemistry, biomechanics, pharmacology and methods of physiotherapy. Third-year topics include rehabilitation after nervous diseases, internal medicine, motor control, massage, musculoskeletal disorders and aquatic physiotherapy, and year four adds geriatrics, paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology applications, research methods and a final examination. Over 1,200 hours of clinical practice take place in hospitals, family medicine centres and rehabilitation facilities. Graduates work in hospitals, clinics, rehabilitation, sports organisations and private practice, or continue to a master's.

name: Oral Hygiene
overview: Early years cover natural sciences, human anatomy, physiology, communication psychology, oral health and personal hygiene, ethics and ergonomics, with a phantom course in professional dental hygiene. Later years add professional dental hygiene, cariology, periodontology, oral surgery with pain control, pharmacology, radiology and prevention, then paediatric dentistry, oral care for older people and orthodontic patients, and an introduction to prosthetic dentistry, each with clinical practice. Teaching is problem-based, with simulation equipment, small clinical groups and Erasmus+ exchange. Graduates advise patients on prevention, run oral health promotion programmes and practise in public or private institutions.

name: Medical and Veterinary Genetics
overview: Human and animal physiology and basic genetics start the degree, followed by general and molecular pathology, molecular biology, biostatistics, immunology and plant genetics, then veterinary genetics, medical genetics, analytical chemistry and bioinformatics. A bachelor thesis runs through the last two years with professional practice in year four. Teaching is problem-based, with work in renovated laboratories and Erasmus+ exchange possible. Graduates work in diagnostic and research laboratories, healthcare and veterinary settings, biotechnology, pharmaceutical and food safety sectors, and environmental protection, or continue to a master's or PhD.

name: Medical and Veterinary Biochemistry
overview: Year one lays foundations in biology, genetics, physics, general, organic and bioorganic chemistry, mathematics and anatomy. Years two and three cover biochemistry, physiology, microbiology, pathology, histology, molecular biology, biotechnology and genetic engineering, laboratory haematology, immunology, bioinformatics and diagnostic biochemistry, and the last year is professional practice and a final thesis. Teaching is problem-based, in renovated laboratories with Erasmus+ exchange possible. Graduates work in biochemical laboratories and private companies on disease diagnostics, environmental monitoring and food analysis, or continue to graduate programmes in laboratory diagnostics and natural sciences.

name: Health Psychology
overview: Year one starts with introduction to psychology, communication, neurophysiology, statistics and human ecology, then health, developmental and cognitive psychology with quantitative and qualitative research methods. Later you study clinical, social and educational psychology, crisis and disaster psychology, psychological assessment, psychiatry and health care systems, and finally counselling, work and organisational and rehabilitation psychology, behavioural medicine and health policy, ending with a bachelor's thesis. Coursework, practice and Erasmus+ exchange are part of the study. Graduates work as assistant psychologists, research or HR assistants in health, social, educational and organisational settings, or continue to a master's.

name: Business Management and Startup Building
overview: Year one teaches the lean start-up method, the lean business model canvas, Google Sprint and design thinking, together with business fundamentals, idea validation and pitching. Year two adds technical and analytical skills, sales techniques and customer acquisition, and you build a minimum viable product and test it with real customers. In year three you scale the venture into an operating company and prepare it for investors, ending at a Demo Day. Core subjects include programming, digital product design, finance, cybersecurity, digital marketing and business law, with mentors and partners such as Startup Lithuania. Graduates become product owners, business developers, digital marketers and founders.

name: Global Business and Modern Marketing
overview: Over three years you study management, micro- and macroeconomics, business statistics and mathematics, human resource management, marketing and market research, business databases and analysis, entrepreneurship, social media marketing, international trade, brand management, project management and business risk management, plus a professional foreign language (English, French or German). Electives include business psychology, leadership, sales management, intercultural management and social entrepreneurship. The final year has an internship and a bachelor thesis, and Erasmus+ exchanges are encouraged. Graduates work in business management, banks, companies and government institutions.

name: Communication and Digital Marketing
overview: Over six semesters you study communication theory, public relations, journalism in the era of disinformation, digital and social network marketing, data analytics, creative writing and advertising texts, digital advertising design, gamification, e-business, startups, electronic publishing, ethics, law and crisis communication, with English, French or German. Projects and creative management and leadership methods are woven in, a fifth-semester internship comes first, and a term paper and bachelor thesis end the degree. Erasmus+ study or internships abroad are possible. Graduates work as SEO and SEM specialists, public relations specialists, content managers and marketers.

name: Law and Global Security
overview: The foundation is constitutional, criminal, civil, administrative, international public and EU law, with theory of law and a professional foreign language. On top come security-focused courses: terrorism and Europe's security, migration and trafficking, anti-corruption instruments, human security law and AI, energy security law, armed conflicts law, cyber security and AI, anti-money laundering, environmental law and intellectual property theft. Teaching uses lectures, seminars, mooting, gamification and talks by experts, and you meet partner organisations from national and international bodies. The final year has a substantial internship and a thesis. Graduates work in human rights, compliance, anti-money laundering and energy or other security roles.

name: Psychology
overview: Seven semesters run from general psychology, philosophy, logic and human anatomy and physiology through perception, memory, learning, thinking and language, to clinical, organisational, educational, forensic and health psychology, with psychopathology, neuropsychology, human genetics, psychological testing, research methods and statistics. Communication skills training, observation and survey skills and psychophysiological measurement laboratories build practice. The final semester has an internship, and a bachelor thesis is supervised individually. Partners include the military, child protection services and correctional departments. Graduates work in social work, human resources and therapy, or continue to doctoral study.

name: English for Specific Purposes and the Second Foreign Language
overview: English phonetics, morphology and syntax, linguistics and literary analysis are combined with English for specific purposes in four domains (business, public administration, law and finance), translation, corpus-driven analysis and terminology research. A second foreign language is studied for six semesters from French, German, Spanish, Norwegian, Chinese or Korean. The final year has professional practice and a bachelor thesis, and Erasmus+ exchange allows study and internships at European or Asian universities. Graduates work in culture and information centres, media, publishing, tourism, translation agencies, international organisations and state departments.

name: English for Specific Purposes and Korean Studies
overview: English studies (phonetics, morphology, syntax, corpus-driven lexicology, discourse analysis, literary analysis, academic writing and translation basics) are paired with four semesters of Korean and electives on Korean reading, conversation and history, plus English for business, public administration, law and finance. One semester is spent on Korean studies in South Korea or at a partner university in Europe in year three. A term paper, professional practice and a bachelor thesis finish the degree, and Korean is taught through the King Sejong Institute in Vilnius. Graduates work in translation, public administration, international organisations and tourism offices.

name: Digital Media Design
overview: The first years combine contemporary mathematics, Python programming, object-oriented design, data structures and databases with computer graphics, matte painting, 3D modelling and animation, motion graphics, cinematography and editing, web design, game design, human-centered design and visual effects, with two years of Korean. Two years are spent in Lithuania and two at Dongseo University in South Korea, where two capstone design internships and a two-part bachelor thesis fall in the later years. Graduates work in TV and production companies, motion graphics studios, virtual reality, 3D modelling, game development and UI and UX design.

name: Game Development and Digital Animation
overview: The degree covers contemporary mathematics, Python, object-oriented design, data structures, databases, AI programming and game engine architectures, with figure drawing, computer graphics, 3D Maya modelling, character animation, compositing, lighting and rendering, game design, level design and 2D and 3D game programming, plus Korean. After year two you lean toward Game Development or Animation and VFX. You design a game from scratch and make your own game as a final project, with two capstone design internships and a bachelor thesis in year four. Two years are at Dongseo University in South Korea. Graduates work in computer games, film, advertising, art and design.

name: Painting
overview: Studio practice in painting and interdisciplinary expression is the centre of the degree, driven by creative projects and an experimental, critical approach to artistic search. Art history, philosophy and cultural studies run alongside, helping you read artworks, understand stylistic movements and place your own work within contemporary art processes. Graduates work in the visual arts, take part in interdisciplinary art projects or curate, and can continue to master's study.

name: Sculpture
overview: You learn to define your own field of interest and to make sculptures, objects for interior and public spaces, installations in contemporary art spaces or specific sites, performances, and light, sound and media works. Communication skills, presenting ideas in written and spoken form, and an understanding of art theory and the institutions that manage art are part of the training. The degree is offered as Sculpture in Vilnius and as Applied Sculpture in Telsiai. Graduates work as independent sculptors or continue to a second-cycle degree.

name: Ceramics
overview: The focus is contemporary artistic ceramics: functional ceramics, ceramic design, and decorative and conceptual work, learned through plastic expression, decoration, firing methods and techniques, with visual composition and spatial relationships. Creative projects and self-study build your own practice. Graduates work independently or in teams, take commissions for public and private spaces, join local and international art projects, work in ceramics manufacture and galleries, or teach in secondary schools and youth art studios, and may continue to master's study.

name: 3D Objects of Art: Glass, Sculpture and Ceramics
overview: You choose one of three specialities, ceramics, glass or sculpture, and learn it in a studio environment through practical workshops in moulding, casting and ceramic firing, combined with digital tools such as computer graphics, Photoshop drawing, Zbrush rendering and Cinema 4D visualisation and animation. Art theory, art history and management support the practice, and creative projects tie it together. Graduates work as professional artists and creators of three-dimensional objects, in creative agencies and across culture and the creative economy, or continue to a master's at home or abroad.

name: Graphic Art
overview: You work in traditional and contemporary printmaking (lithography, woodcut, linocut, etching, silkscreen, photogravure, offset lithography and digital printing), typography, calligraphy, illustration, publication design and bookbinding, with art history, theory and philosophy. In years three and four you concentrate on printmaking, illustration or book art through intensive creative work and conceptual visual art projects. Exchanges through Erasmus and Nord Plus are encouraged. Graduates become illustrators, book artists, creative staff in design and advertising agencies, art editors, curators or independent artists, and can continue to a master's.

name: Applied Graphics
overview: The degree covers classical and modern graphic technologies and social and conceptual graphic art, including stamping, book design, poster creation, illustration, calligraphy, typography and digital art, set in the context of art theory, history, philosophy and management. After the first year you choose applied graphics, illustration or digital art. The department brings in visiting artists, including from Sweden, Norway and the United States, for intensive workshops, and students take part in exhibitions in Lithuania and abroad. Graduates work in publishing, visual communication, illustration and posters, or continue to a master's or doctoral study.

name: Graphic Design
overview: The programme centres on graphic and communication design: designing and presenting images, identities and visual information across traditional, virtual and interactive media. It keeps close links with European design schools and Lithuanian enterprises. Graduates apply skills in managing visual information and software, work individually or in teams or start their own business, and can continue to second-cycle study in graphic design, design management or other design fields.

name: Design
overview: The course joins practical, experimental design activity with design research, theory classes and professional critique, and teaches you to research and solve functional, socio-cultural or economic problems with a grounding in research work. Student projects have won international design awards and become real company products. The degree is offered as Furniture Design and Product Design in Telsiai, Product Design in Vilnius and General Design in Vilnius and Kaunas. Graduates work as product designers in studios, companies or freelance, in fields such as furniture, transport, consumer electronics, medical equipment, accessories and packaging.

name: Interior Design
overview: You study interior design fundamentals with architecture and fine arts basics, design and finishing materials and technologies, lighting techniques, construction physics and visual expression methods, together with art history, philosophy, psychology, social communication and foreign languages. Teaching is interactive and problem-oriented, with team projects with social partners, the chance to work with scenography specialists in theatre, cinema and television, and practice presenting to specialist and general audiences. Graduates work independently on interiors, in architecture and design teams or as consultants for firms in furniture, lighting and materials, and can continue to a master's in spatial design.

name: Fashion Design
overview: You study costume design, fashion drawing, colour science, twentieth-century fashion history, AutoCAD design, material structures, fashion forecasting and artistic expression techniques. The programme gives students freedom to choose from many topics and works closely with fashion industry enterprises, so skills can be tested in practice during the studies. Graduates work as costume designers in clothing industries, trade companies, theatres, film studios, television and the press, and with extra pedagogical qualifications can teach in schools and art schools.

name: Textile and Fashion
overview: The focus is textile art and design, with surface design of fabrics, the surface formation of woven fabrics, fashion accessories and textile objects in architectural settings, supported by practical skills in textile technologies. Studio learning and project work prepare you to solve creative tasks independently and to collaborate with architects, interior designers and customers. Graduates create fabrics and accessories for fashion, work in the fashion and light industries, carry out community creative projects or build an individual artistic practice.

name: Metal Art and Jewelry
overview: The degree is practice-based and research-informed, with studio work at its core and experimentation with materials, metal and jewellery techniques, sustainable material technologies, digital tools and new media, and traditional hand skills. Body-object-space thinking, interdisciplinary and installation approaches and theory in contemporary art and design discourse complete the study. Graduates become independent jewellery and metal artists, contemporary jewellery designers, workshop leaders, cultural project developers or creative entrepreneurs, and can continue to a master's in art or design.

name: Photography and Media Art
overview: Work spans photography, videography, sound and new media, from analogue photography to hybrid media and interdisciplinary art practice, set alongside art theory. Teaching is studio-based, with creative and technological workshops, individual and collective projects, exhibitions, seminars and meetings with professionals, plus traineeships and Erasmus mobility. You learn to formulate artistic goals, analyse creative work and present it to specialists and general audiences. Graduates work independently, in creative industries such as advertising, visual design, television and cinema, or continue to a master's.

name: Site-specific Art (fresco-mosaic, stained glass)
overview: You learn fresco casting, sgraffito carving, direct and reverse mosaic and classical stained glass methods (including Tiffany), alongside academic drawing (still life, portrait, anatomy) and easel painting in watercolour and oil. The first two years build technique and lead into one of two tracks, Fresco-Mosaic or Stained Glass, and years three and four develop a personal practice and its place in public space. Graduates work independently, exhibit and join residencies, symposiums and festivals, create public installations and collaborate with architects and designers.

name: Architecture (Integrated Studies)
overview: The five-year integrated degree combines general education (aesthetics, philosophy of art, art history, mathematics) with construction techniques, building materials, construction physics, urban planning, heritage conservation, sustainable architecture, twentieth-century architecture history and computerised design methods, plus drawing and painting. Applied research and design projects make research the starting point of the creative process, and architectural composition, building design, structural design and environmental planning form the specialist core. Professional practice and a final project close the degree. Graduates work in architectural firms, planning institutions and government agencies, and can become project leaders after two years of practice.

name: Dance: Classical
note: One overview for the Dance card (classical and contemporary share one study plan).
overview: You specialise in classical or contemporary dance, and both follow the same plan. Through most of the degree you work in dance praxis and creation alongside dance theory and discourses, with voice and acting praxis, sound and space contexts, and professional sustainability and practice running throughout. Philosophy, aesthetics, project management and the psychology of art and creativity give the wider context. The degree ends with a final art project that you defend.

name: Dance: Contemporary
note: Takes out the near-duplicate overview: the Dance card has one, on its classical path.
